evidence_boundaries: The Hall-thruster PRE is a formally published, large-scale author 3D PIC/MCC study; its transport maps are not experiments, and the absolute amplitude and late-time structure are not fully grid converged.
The KSTAR study directly classifies microwave gas breakdown with D-alpha signals, while the Brownian-transport mechanism and ITER 1 MW projection are model results.
The KSTAR validation is a boundary comparison within roughly a factor of two in pressure and does not validate post-breakdown burn-through, closed-flux formation, or current ramp-up.
The slow-positron paper is a workshop preprint based on Geant4-Penelope plus an empirical diffusion model; it reports no new measured slow-positron flux.
The slow-positron driver is a conventional 65 MeV electron linac, so transfer to laser-accelerated electron beams requires new phase-space, heat-load, and transport calculations.
No AlgoPlasma/PMSL, BREAK, FIST99, MolFlow+, G4beamline, Geant4, neutral-gas, thermal, or beam-optics calculation was rerun locally.
